metadata.title: Seven Things That Changed
metadata.purpose: Walk viewers through the seven prompting shifts required for Opus 4.7 — from naming scope and defining length to using action verbs and unlocking maximum reasoning.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

props.command: What is: Seven Things That Changed?

beats.narration_text: Nǐ hǎo. This is Liam, in for Bear. Are you still prompting Claude the same way you did six months ago? Opus 4.7 changed the rules. Here are the seven shifts that matter.

props.ask: How should I prompt Claude Opus 4.7 differently than before?
props.answer_preview: Opus 4.7 does exactly what you type. Name every output, define length...
props.command: Are you still prompting Claude the same way you did six months ago?

beats.narration_text: Seven shifts. One: name every output, name the order, name the scope — 4.7 does exactly what you typed, not what you meant. Two: define length explicitly — if you want a short summary, say so; 4.7 sizes the answer to what it thinks the task is. Three: use positive instructions only — negative instructions stick to the literal sentence and do not generalize. Four: use action verbs only — each verb tells 4.7 to ship something specific, and it loves that.

illustration.concept: Shifts 1 through 4 side by side — old vs. new prompting patterns
illustration.layout: Two columns labeled 'Before (4.6)' and 'After (4.7)'. Four rows, one per shift. Each row shows a short old prompt phrase struck through on the left, and a short new prompt phrase on the right. Terracotta highlight on the right column only.

beats.narration_text: Five: tool-calling changed. Before, 4.6 called tools constantly. Now 4.7 reasons more between calls and calls fewer tools. If the output quality is good, trust the new default. If you need more tool use, ask for it explicitly. Six: the tone is more direct — less validation, almost no emojis. If you want warmth back, paste two or three sentences in the voice you want and tell Claude to match the rhythm.

illustration.concept: Shifts 5 and 6 — tool-calling and tone changes
illustration.layout: Two horizontal panels stacked. Top panel: '5 Tool-calling' — left side shows 'frequent calls' icon, right side shows 'reason → fewer calls' with a thinking icon. Bottom panel: '6 Tone' — left shows emoji cluster, right shows clean text with 'direct' label. Terracotta separator line between panels.

beats.narration_text: Seven: for creative or open-ended tasks, add the phrase: go beyond the basics. This phrase comes from Anthropic's own documentation on 4.7. It pushes the model past the literal minimum and into genuinely interesting territory. Try it once and you will never leave it out again.

card.sub: Phrase from Anthropic's 4.7 docs — unlocks creative depth

beats.narration_text: Bonus: 4.7 has adaptive thinking — it reasons before answering, but only when it decides to. If you want maximum reasoning every time, add this phrase at the end of your prompt: Think before answering, maximum reasoning. The author reports this consistently produces better results. Treat it as a technique to test, not a guaranteed Anthropic feature.

There is one more layer. Claude supports custom skills — slash commands with pre-built instructions. You can build a skill that takes any lazy prompt and converts it into a 4.7-optimized one. The author calls his slash 47. You type a rough idea, the skill rewrites it as a structured prompt, you copy it, paste it into a new chat, and get a much better output.

card.sub: A /skill that upgrades any rough prompt to 4.7 structure

beats.narration_text: The full checklist — name scope, define length, positive only, action verbs, trust tool defaults, request tone, go beyond the basics — takes thirty seconds to internalize. Pick one shift. Rewrite one prompt you use every week. Notice what changes. Then add the next shift.

card.sub: Pick the change that matches your most repeated task

beats.narration_text: Take one prompt you use every week. Rewrite it with shift one: name the exact output, name the order, name the scope. Run it. Compare the result. If you want a shortcut, build or download a prompt-optimizer skill that does the rewrite for you.

card.sub: Name the output, order, and scope — then compare results

beats.narration_text: Seven shifts. One model. The prompts that worked on 4.6 are not wrong — they are just underspecified for what 4.7 can do. Specify more. Get more. This is Liam, in for Bear.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you've been prompting Claude for a while and you feel like you're doing it wrong — getting inconsistent results, fighting with it, rewriting the same things. Ask Claude to show you the seven prompt behaviors that most commonly changed between when people learned prompting and now, and which of the seven is most likely responsible for inconsistent outputs.
